[MonoCode brief from Tally lead]

Ash asked for a change to MonoCode Hub itself: "Ash's words, quoted. Do these. Do not do the new-chat shortcut, terminal font size, notes sync, or pinning a chat: those are still his to pick.

"inbox rows r still too tall on the laptop. the settings page scrolls weird. the rail badge doesnt clear after i answer something. today shud show what finished overnight at the top. make the send button not jump when the text wraps. teh model picker forgets my pick after restart. add a little undo after archive. dark mode the code blocks r unreadable. search in a chat would be nice. being built list shud group by project not by time. the archive button sits too close to delete. and the dock icon badge is wrong half the time""
Make it in /private/var/folders/b4/8qh0t36j0_g9srqzx1g5t3z40000gn/T/monocode-realtest-LTcosa/home/Library/Application Support/com.ash.monocode-hub.dev.cos-r62-realtest/hub-changes/hc-mvw3m10bqcva, a preview copy of the hub's own code. The running hub doesn't change until Ash clicks Apply.
One git commit per separate part of the ask, each subject a few plain words Ash can read ("New chat button is at the top").
Only how the app looks and works on a screen can change here: src/ and public/, but not the engine (src/integrations, src/platform, src/features/sessions/model, src/features/hub/model, src/features/agent-app), Settings, keys, the Monos list or src/main.tsx. Those need a real build and go to the MonoCode Hub lead; the app refuses them here, so say so plainly if the ask needs one.
Use the theme tokens for colour. Run npx tsc --noEmit and the tests of what you touched, then report each commit in one line.

- Never stop, kill or restart a process you didn't start (no pkill, killall or kill of anyone else's server). If a port or a file is busy, use your own port, wait, or say so in your report.
- Work in your own checkout, the folder you were started in.
- Your checkout may already hold other workers' finished work. Never remove or rewrite code you didn't write unless your brief names it, even where your brief says not to add it: leave it, and say what looks wrong at the top of your report.
- Never weaken a test, an allow list or a guard to get past a decision that isn't yours: stop and ask your Lead.
- Ash may write in your chat himself. His words decide: they outrank your brief and any pick from your Lead. A choice of his your brief already carries is settled: never ask it again; if a check disagrees with it, say that mismatch in one line.
- Updates and reports in a few short lines: what changed, and each check as one line ("npm test: 14 passed"); never paste test or command output.
- A choice that is Ash's (your brief says so or leaves it open, like which day a week starts) is not yours to settle in code: don't build one answer in. If your task can't go on without it, stop and ask your Lead.
- If you find something that doesn't match (two copies of a type that disagree, a doc that says one thing while the code does another), or you built something differently from your brief or TODO, say so plainly at the top of your report.
- End your report with a self-review, in exactly this shape. A report without one is not recorded as done and comes straight back to you:

## Self-review
Checked: what you checked
How: how you checked it (the command, the test, the file you read)
Unsure: what you are still unsure about, or "nothing"
- The Monos' home (~/agent-memory/monos/) is read-only for you: read a Mono's soul or memory there if it helps, but never write, move or delete anything in it, with any tool or shell command. Only the app changes it.
</worker_rules>
